text:
mira: quick heads-up — while onboarding magnet-40b-quant3 I hit a consistent quality regression after very long prefill (>36k tokens). appears related to KV evaporation during prefill shrink.

oliver: where did you run this? cloud or local? any quick repro?

mira: ran on a dedicated 2xA100 slot and replicated on hosted sandbox. minimal repro attached below. runs clean at 16k/32k but diverges past ~36k. seed included.

jen: can you paste the tiny repro cmd?

mira: sure:
```
python infra/run_long_prefill.py --model magnet-40b-quant3 --tokens 38000 --seed 49201 --dump=fprefix.json
```
behavior: model logits diverge shortly after an eviction event; sampling paths change and BLEU-style recall drops ~5-7 points vs fp baseline.

sam: perf-bot, any recent changes to kvcache eviction heuristics?

perf-bot: snapshot for job=longprefill-1749:
- kvcache.evictions.count: 12
- kvcache.last_eviction.reason: shrink_on_pressure
- kvcache.shed_prefixes: 14
- kvcache.fingerprint.mismatch_events: 3
- runtime.quant.memcpy.strategy: stride_aligned_v2

oliver: looks like the eviction + quant memcpy/stride path might be miscomputing position offsets when a prefix is removed and later re-infused. RoPE offsets could be getting remapped incorrectly in the quantized key/value layout.

mira: I diffed logits around the first mismatch point. tiny excerpt:
```
# index ~36502
fp_logits = [1.92, -0.44, 0.01, 0.87]
quant3_logits = [0.05, -2.11, -0.33, 0.12]
```

jen: did you try disabling the OOM-evict fast-path?

mira: yes: disable-oom-evict -> no mismatch. enable + fallback-to-fp for memcpy -> no mismatch. suggests quant memcpy path + eviction interaction.

sam: can you capture a kv dump pre/post eviction (hashes + positions)? we need to check if the pos indices in the quant packing align with expectations.

mira: uploaded kv dumps to the ticket: kv_before.bin, kv_after.bin, and fp_trace.json. also added seed/prompt.

oliver: action plan proposal:
1) Add a targeted unit test that runs a synthetic prefill that simulates eviction and asserts fingerprint continuity for quant variants.
2) Add an assert in the memcpy kernel that checks stride/offset sanity when copying from src->dst during shrink/resize (safe-early-fail in debug builds).
3) Canary: If any long-prefill job sees kvcache.shed_prefixes > 0 AND model is quantized, fallback the request to FP variant for first 1k tokens post-prefill and emit a regression alert.

jen: i'll start on 1) and 3) — add the canary flag behind a feature toggle so we can roll it back quickly.

sam: i'll instrument memcpy/stride logging at debug level and kick a bake run on a dedicated pool. also open an infra rollback ticket to pin a working kernel if needed.

mira: tiny note: the divergence consistently begins at roughly the same absolute token index (around 36,500). that feels like a deterministic remap rather than random noise.

oliver: could be an integer wrap or index truncation in the quant index math. check all places that compute pos_idx % window_size with int casts.

jen: added failing test to PR #3421 with test vector + kv dump. keeping it small so CI runs quickly but still triggers the eviction path via a mock.

sam: i ran a longprefill with forced-evict on dedicated-qa and confirmed fingerprint mismatch reproduces. attaching logs.

mira: thanks. i'll file a short postmortem note for the bring-up doc and include mitigation checklist: canary, kernel assert, nightly longprefill added to the regression matrix. tagging docs-bot to surface the mitigation in the onboarding guide.

docs-bot: noted. will add a "Long-prefill eviction risks" section to model-onboarding.md and link the PRs.

oliver: ok folks — assign to @jen (canary + tests) and @sam (kernel instruments). i'll take the bisect on memcpy stride code tomorrow.

mira: appreciate it. seed=49201, prompt attached to ticket. moving this to assigned. :thumbsup:
